paragraphs: Mentioned in a baraita, [Sanhedrin 4a (Hyman cites 7a)](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.4a.4), and in [Sifra, Tazria, chapter 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Sifra%2C_Tazria_Parashat_Yoledet%2C_Chapter_2.2). His students asked Rabbi Yehudah ben Ro'etz, ‘Shall I read “seventy”—’; he answered them, ‘He declared impure and pure in the case of male birth [supplied בוכר], etc.’[^1][^2][^3]

notes.text: [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1650&lang=en) gives Sanhedrin 4a and Sifra, Tazria, chapter 2. Both linked passages give Rabbi Yehudah ben Ro’etz’s students asking about reading “seventy.”
The linked witnesses give male birth in the comparison that follows. Hyman quotes only the opening of the discussion.

Sifra, Tazria, Parashat Yoledet 2:2 and Sanhedrin 4a both give the students’ question about reading “seventy” and the comparison with male birth. The photographed Hyman notice cites Sanhedrin 7a, abbreviates the exchange, and appears to read בזכר at the point represented by בוכר in the supplied transcription.
